source_text: Si enim incolumissima fide, scholari more ad ostendendas tantummodo eruditionis tuae vires, ea tentares quae sunt invicta concutere; finito tamen certaminis ludicro, his quibus obloquebaris palmam daturus; probaremus litterarum studium, sed irreligiosum castigaremus exemplum. Porro cum dogma nec verisimilitudinis corrupto saltem colore perfusum, quod nullis legis testimoniis (quippe numquam rationi praeiudicantibus) potestis tueri, et hoc tamen impietate sua horrens, stultitia iacens, nusquam nisi inter inguina voluntatum, honestate, disputatione, sacraque lege confossum, turpissima obstinatione secteris; consequitur ex tribus unum, ut aut plumbei ad intellegendum acuminis, aut maleficii illius quod Manichaeorum mysteriis teneri, fando accepimus, catenas, aut utrumque simul perpeti iudiceris.
pass_a_gloss: For if with a most unharmed faith, in a school manner for showing only the powers of your learning, you were trying to shake those things which are unconquered; yet, the sport of the contest having been finished, about to give the palm to those whom you were contradicting; we would approve the study of letters, but we would chastise the irreligious example. Further, when you follow with most foul obstinacy a dogma not even poured over with a corrupted color of likelihood, which you cannot protect by any testimonies of the law (seeing that they never prejudge reason), and this nevertheless shuddering by its own impiety, lying by stupidity, nowhere except among the groins of wills, pierced through by honorableness, by disputation, and by the sacred law; it follows one of three things, that you are judged either of leaden sharpness for understanding, or to suffer the chains of that crime which we have received by report to be held in the mysteries of the Manichaeans, or both at once.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: For if, with your faith entirely intact, you were attempting to shake what cannot be defeated merely to show the strength of your learning, in the manner of a school exercise, while intending to award the victory to those you opposed once the playful contest ended, I would approve your literary enthusiasm but rebuke your irreligious example. Instead, you follow with the ugliest stubbornness a doctrine that lacks even the false coloring of plausibility and that you cannot defend by any testimonies of the Law, since these never count against reason. It bristles with impiety and lies prostrate in foolishness, existing nowhere except amid the groins of human desires, pierced through by decency, argument, and sacred law. One of three conclusions therefore follows: either your understanding is leaden, or you suffer the chains of that sorcery we have heard is contained in the Manichaean mysteries, or both at once.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
